title: Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Medical Group customers
content_md: SBC Medical Group has warned in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that two cybersecurity incidents exposed sensitive customer and employee information, including personal data belonging to 1.6 million people. SBC Medical Group is a clinic management company whose main business is in Japan , but it also has a limited presence in the U.S., is traded on Nasdaq as SBC, and holds a minority stake in the medical spa chain OrangeTwist. Its clinics receive 7 million patient visits annually. The first compromise concerns the SBC databases, while the second involves unauthorized access to clinic administrator accounts on Tribeau, a third-party booking platform. The company discovered the database breach on November 16 and was notified of the Tribeau compromise the same day. Both incidents affected its Japan-based businesses. "On November 16, 2026, unauthorized access occurred to certain databases within a website system managed and operated by SBC Medical Group, Ltd., the Company’s, Japanese subsidiary, in connection with its management services in Japan," reads a FORM 8-K filing with the SEC. "The Company confirmed that an unauthorized third party accessed and extracted customer information. The method of intrusion and full scope remain under investigation."
